items.title: Dawoud Sabu Adeyola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 30, 2025
items.q: Like Albert Ayler said, music is the healing force of the universe. I love that quote from him too.

ctx.x: Yes. And it made me wonder what you hope listeners get from your music? I don’t know if I could have phrased that in a better way, but do you hope — I think you know what I mean.

Yeah. I think my answer would be similar to what John Coltrane was asked a similar question one time and I loved his answer. He said, “I hope to make people realize that we live in a big beautiful universe. We are only a tiny part of a beautiful universe and that I will hope that my listeners realize that there is meaning to life. Life has meaning and certainly life does have meaning, and that this meaning can be expressed through music. And something like that he said. And I always thought that that was really…

That’s a good one. I’ve heard people say and write about free jazz, because you mentioned Albert Ayler — a lot of times it seems like why are these musicians so angry. And I once asked Rashied Ali about that and he said it was more about just a reflection of the times. I wonder if you have a thought about that?
